ins.intro: Cross-checks of what managers entered. These are leads for who to talk to first, not scores or rankings. Only HR sees cross-team results.
ins.convTitle: Talk to these people first: career conversations
ins.convNote: Medium or High retention risk, and nobody has discussed their career aspirations yet. A 15-minute conversation is the cheapest, fastest retention action.
ins.unlistedNote: Other managers name them as Ready Now or 1-2 years successors, but their own manager has not listed them as key talent. Worth confirming in calibration.
ins.more: {{count}} more; use export or filters to see them
ins.fragileTitle: Covered on paper, fragile in practice
ins.fragileNote: A critical role whose near-ready successor is at Medium or High retention risk. Both people could leave together; keeping the successor protects two roles.
ins.matchNote: Critical roles with a thin bench or a TBH successor, matched to people whose own next role is that job and who are ready soon. Talk to them before opening the requisition.
ins.calNote: These describe how the form was filled in, not anyone’s quality. When they appear, the HRBP may want to ask one more question. Teams with 4 or more key talents only.

sig.sameReadiness: everyone has the same next-role readiness
sig.vaguePlans: most plans have a very thin evaluation method
sig.noTbhAllReady: every successor is Ready Now and there is no TBH

ins.supplyTitle: Internal mobility supply vs. external hiring need
ins.supplyNote: Per department: key talents open to moving soon, against critical roles that need an outside hire. Where supply is enough, consider internal moves first.
